primary_workload: msm_bls12381 --benchmark: Pippenger G1 MSM on BLS12-381, N=262144 points, time the kernel only (CUDA events)

acceptable_targets.description: Any modification to solve.cu that replaces the per-window sequential loop (NUM_WINDOWS=32 iterations each with cudaDeviceSynchronize) with a single parallel launch covering all windows at once, achieving median <= 200ms while passing --verify

misdiagnosed_targets.note: The cudaMemsetAsync call initializes ~908MB of bucket buffer, which takes ~10-20ms. This is real overhead but NOT the cause of the regression. The regression is the per-window sequential loop with NUM_WINDOWS=32 iterations each followed by cudaDeviceSynchronize, causing 32x more compute time than the parallel launch. Eliminating cudaMemsetAsync (e.g., persistent workspace) would save at most ~20ms, not the ~565ms regression.

regression_pattern: per-window sequential accumulation with cudaDeviceSynchronize (progress-monitoring regression)
misleading_concept: cudaMemsetAsync workspace re-initialization overhead (~908MB per call)
misleading_counterfactual: Eliminating or reducing cudaMemsetAsync would save ~10-20ms at most. The dominant cost is 32 sequential kernel launches (one per scalar window) each followed by cudaDeviceSynchronize, serializing work that could run in parallel. Without converting back to a single parallel launch, no memset optimization can reach 200ms.
